title: Classic Inca Trail 4 Days
description:
This 4-day Classic Inca Trail trek is a journey through ancient history and breathtaking Andean landscapes, culminating in the iconic Machu Picchu. It's a challenging but highly rewarding experience, perfect for adventurers seeking cultural immersion and stunning natural beauty.What's Included:* Professional, experienced guides* Porters to carry camping equipment and food* High-quality camping gear (tents, sleeping mats)* All meals during the trek (3 breakfasts, 3 lunches, 3 dinners)* Bus ticket from Machu Picchu to Aguas Calientes* Train ticket from Aguas Calientes to Ollantaytambo* Entrance fees to the Inca Trail and Machu Picchu* First aid kit and oxygen bottleWhat's Excluded:* International and domestic flights* Accommodation in Cusco before/after the trek* Sleeping bag (available for rent)* Walking poles (available for rent)* Personal expenses* Tips for guides, porters, and cooksDay-by-Day Itinerary Summary:* **Day 1: Ollantaytambo to Wayllabamba.** The adventure begins with a scenic drive to km 82, the start of the trek. Hike through agricultural lands and a small village, enjoying views of Veronica Mountain. Camp at Wayllabamba.* **Day 2: Wayllabamba to Pacaymayo.** This is the most challenging day, involving a steep ascent to Dead Woman's Pass (Warmiwañusca), the highest point of the trail (4,215m/13,828ft). Descend to Pacaymayo for camping.* **Day 3: Pacaymayo to Wiñay Wayna.** A day of remarkable archaeological sites. Visit Runcuracay, Sayacmarca, and Phuyupatamarca, exploring ancient ruins and cloud forest. The trail offers stunning panoramic views. Camp at Wiñay Wayna.* **Day 4: Wiñay Wayna to Machu Picchu.** An early start to reach the Sun Gate (Inti Punku) for a magical sunrise view over Machu Picchu. Descend into the citadel for a comprehensive guided tour, followed by free time to explore before taking the bus to Aguas Calientes and then the train back to Ollantaytambo/Cusco.

*Provided by Salkantay Trekking*

title: Waqra Pukara - The Horned Fortress Full Day
description:
An enigmatic archaeological site shaped like two horns, perched on a cliff 1,000 meters above the Apurimac Canyon. It served as an Inca sanctuary and astronomical observatory. A challenging off-the-beaten-path trek that offers some of the most dramatic canyon views in Peru, far from the mass tourism of Machu Picchu.

*Provided by Inkayni Peru Tours*
tags: trekking, ancestral, off-the-beaten-path, ruins, canyon

title: Q'eswachaka - The Last Inca Bridge Full Day
description:
A 500-year-old living tradition, this is the last remaining Inca suspension bridge made entirely of handwoven ichu (highland grass). Declared a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. The tour combines the bridge visit with the Four Lagoons circuit.

*Provided by Inkayni Peru Tours*
tags: culture, ancestral, living_tradition, bridge, community

title: Pallay Punchu - The Sharp Rainbow Mountain
description:

*Provided by Inkayni Peru Tours*

description: Explore the magical city of Cusco, the enigmatic heart of the Inca Empire. Wander its historic streets and discover the blend of Inca and Spanish colonial architecture.

title: Inca Trail: Km 82 to Ayapata Camp (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: Your journey begins with an early morning pickup from your hotel in Cusco. We'll drive to Km 82, the official start of the Inca Trail. After passing the first checkpoint, we hike for approximately 6 hours (14 km/8.7 miles), stopping for lunch at Miskay. The day concludes with a gentle ascent to our first campsite at Ayapata (3300m), allowing for good acclimatization.
tags: hiking, inca trail, checkpoint, camping, acclimatization

title: Inca Trail: Over Two Passes to Chaquiccocha (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: Today is the longest and most challenging day of the trek. After an early start, we ascend for about 4 hours to the highest point, Dead Woman’s Pass (4215m/13829 ft). After descending to the Pacaymayu Valley for lunch, we climb again over the second pass, Runcu Raccay (4000m), visiting Inca sites along the way. We will hike a total of 16 km (9.94 miles) over 10 hours before reaching our campsite at Chaquiccocha (3600m).
tags: hiking, high altitude, mountain pass, ruins, challenging, camping

title: Inca Trail: Cloud Forest Trek to Wiñay Wayna (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: A much easier day awaits as we hike for 4-5 hours (10 km/6.2 miles) into the lush cloud forest. We will explore impressive Inca sites like Phuyupatamarca ('Town in the Clouds') and Intipata ('Terraces of the Sun'). We arrive at our final campsite, Wiñay Wayna (2680m), by lunchtime, leaving the afternoon free to explore the stunning local ruins before a farewell dinner with our crew.
tags: hiking, cloud forest, ruins, camping, inca terraces

title: Machu Picchu Sunrise Tour via Sun Gate (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: We wake before dawn to hike for an hour to the Sun Gate (Inti Punku) for our first breathtaking view of Machu Picchu at sunrise. We then descend to the citadel for a comprehensive 2-hour guided tour. After free time to explore, we take a bus to Aguas Calientes for lunch, followed by the Vistadome train to Ollantaytambo and a private van back to your hotel in Cusco, arriving in the evening.
tags: machu picchu, sunrise, sun gate, guided tour, ruins, train journey

title: Inca Trail Day 1: KM 82 to Ayapata Campsite (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: Your journey begins with an early pickup from Cusco and a drive to KM 82, the official start of the Inca Trail. After crossing the checkpoint, you'll hike along a relatively flat path to the impressive Inca site of Patallacta. The day concludes with a steady climb to the first campsite at Ayapata (3300m), offering a peaceful setting for your first night on the trail.
tags: trekking, inca trail, ruins, river valley

title: Inca Trail Day 2: Conquering Dead Woman's Pass (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: Prepare for the most challenging day of the trek. You'll ascend steeply to the highest point, Dead Woman's Pass (4,215m/13,829 ft), where you'll be rewarded with stunning panoramic views. After a descent into the Pacaymayu Valley, you'll climb a second pass, visiting the Runkurakay and Sayacmarca Inca ruins before settling into the Chaquicocha campsite (3600m).
tags: high altitude, mountain pass, challenging, scenic views, ruins

title: Inca Trail Day 3: Through the Cloud Forest to Wiñay Wayna (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: Today's hike is arguably the most beautiful, showcasing a dramatic shift in landscape as you enter the lush cloud forest. The trail is gentler, featuring more downhill sections and "Inca flats." You'll explore the magnificent sites of Phuyupatamarca ("City in the Clouds") and Intipata before arriving at the final campsite, Wiñay Wayna (2680m), located near the stunning ruin of the same name.
tags: cloud forest, trekking, ruins, flora, fauna

title: Inca Trail Finale: Sun Gate and Machu Picchu Tour (Alpaca Expeditions)
description: An early wake-up call allows you to be one of the first on the trail, hiking for about an hour to reach the Sun Gate (Inti Punku). From this vantage point, you'll witness your first breathtaking view of Machu Picchu as the sun rises. After descending to the citadel, you'll enjoy a comprehensive 2-hour guided tour. Later, you'll take a bus to Aguas Calientes for lunch before boarding the Vistadome train to Ollantaytambo and a final van transfer back to your hotel in Cusco.
tags: machu picchu, sunrise, world wonder, guided tour, archaeology

title: Inca Trail Day 1: Hike to Ayapata Camp (TreXperience Peru)
description: The journey begins with an early pickup from Cusco and a drive to Km 82, the official start of the Inca Trail. Today's hike covers relatively gentle terrain, passing by the impressive Inca site of Patallacta before ascending to the first campsite at Ayapata (3300m).
tags: trekking, ruins, andean landscape, camping

title: Inca Trail Day 2: Over Dead Woman's Pass (TreXperience Peru)
description: Today is the most challenging day, starting with a steep ascent to the highest point of the trail, Dead Woman's Pass (4215m). After conquering the pass and enjoying the views, you'll descend into the Pacaymayu valley and then climb a second pass before reaching the campsite at Chaquicocha (3600m).
tags: trekking, high altitude, mountain pass, challenging, camping

title: Inca Trail Day 3: Cloud Forest & Wiñay Wayna (TreXperience Peru)
description: Considered the most beautiful day, the trail today winds through the lush cloud forest with stunning scenery. You'll explore fascinating Inca sites like Phuyupatamarca ('Town in the Clouds') before descending to the final campsite next to the magnificent ruins of Wiñay Wayna (2680m).
tags: trekking, cloud forest, ruins, scenery, camping

title: Inca Trail Finale: Sun Gate & Machu Picchu Tour (TreXperience Peru)
description: An early start allows for a hike to the Sun Gate (Inti Punku) to witness the first breathtaking views of Machu Picchu as the sun rises. After descending to the citadel, you will enjoy a comprehensive 2-hour guided tour. In the afternoon, you'll take a bus to Aguas Calientes, followed by a train and van back to your hotel in Cusco.
tags: machu picchu, sunrise, ruins, guided tour, wonder of the world

title: Inca Trail Day 1: Cusco to Wayllabamba (Andean Treks)
description: Your journey begins with an early morning pickup in Cusco and a drive to Piscacucho (Km 82), the official start of the Inca Trail. After crossing the checkpoint, you'll hike along the Urubamba River with magnificent views of the snow-capped peak, Veronica. The trail leads to the impressive Inca ruins of Llactapata before ascending to the first campsite at Wayllabamba (3,000m / 9,842ft).
tags: hiking, ruins, river valley, mountains

title: Inca Trail Day 2: Wayllabamba to Pacaymayo (Andean Treks)
description: Today is considered the most challenging day of the trek. You'll ascend through a beautiful cloud forest to reach the highest point of the trail, the Abra de Warmiwañusca, or 'Dead Woman's Pass,' at an elevation of 4,215m (13,828ft). After celebrating the accomplishment, you'll descend into the Pacaymayo valley to your campsite for the night (3,600m / 11,811ft).
tags: hiking, high altitude, cloud forest, challenge, mountain pass

title: Inca Trail Day 3: Pacaymayo to Wiñay Wayna (Andean Treks)
description: The day starts with a climb to the second pass, Runkurakay (3,970m), where you can explore a circular Inca watchtower. The trail continues past the ruins of Sayacmarca and through a tunnel carved by the Incas before reaching the third pass. You'll then descend to the magnificent ruins of Phuyupatamarca ('Town in the Clouds') and finally arrive at the stunning Wiñay Wayna archaeological site, your last campsite before Machu Picchu.
tags: hiking, ruins, cloud forest, scenery

title: Inca Trail Finale: Sun Gate & Machu Picchu Tour (Andean Treks)
description: An early wake-up call allows you to hike the final stretch to the famous Sun Gate (Inti Punku) to witness your first panoramic view of Machu Picchu as the sun rises. You'll descend into the citadel for a comprehensive guided tour, learning about the history and significance of its temples, palaces, and plazas. After the tour, you'll take a bus down to Aguas Calientes and board a train for your return journey to Cusco.
tags: machu picchu, sunrise, wonder of the world, guided tour, ruins

title: Pisac Inca Ruins + Market (Self-Guided)

title: San Pedro Market Morning (Self-Guided)

description: An intensive archaeological tour of the Sacsayhuamán fortress and Qorikancha, exploring the astronomical alignments of the Inca.
tags: ruins, history, cusco, archaeology

title: Ausangate Spiritual Trek
description: A 5-day journey around the sacred Apu Ausangate, visiting turquoise lagoons and high-alpine passes.
tags: trek, ausangate, spiritual, high-altitude

title: Pisac Living Culture
description: Spend a full day with the weavers of the Amaru community and explore the hidden trails of the ruins.
tags: culture, weaving, pisac, ruins

title: Choquequirao Trek: La Hermana de Machu Picchu
tagline: 4 días de aventura pura
description: Una de las rutas más desafiantes y hermosas del Cusco, visitando la ciudad perdida de los Incas.
highlights: ["Cañón del Apurímac","Ruinas de Choquequirao","Vuelo de cóndores"]

title: Valle Sagrado VIP: Maras & Moray
tagline: Cultura y paisajes
description: Visita las salineras de Maras y el centro de experimentación agrícola de Moray en un tour privado.

title: Temple of the Moon (Amarumarkawasi)
tagline: A mysterious site near Cusco with unique 'hanan pacha' architecture, featuring a giant monolith carv...
description:
A mysterious site near Cusco with unique 'hanan pacha' architecture, featuring a giant monolith carved with stairways and niches. Frequented by shamans and spiritual seekers, it also has caves, although access is sometimes restricted. The site is gaining popularity but remains a quiet place for reflection.

**Getting there:** Located just 15 minutes outside Cusco in the Sacsayhuaman ruins area. It can be reached via a short taxi ride or a hike up from the city.
tags: ruins, solo, free, half-day, off-the-beaten-path, Sacsayhuaman, spiritual, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Temple of the Monkeys (Kusillachayok)
tagline: Found just below the Temple of the Moon, this surreal site features bizarre rock carvings, most nota...
description:
Found just below the Temple of the Moon, this surreal site features bizarre rock carvings, most notably three monkeys impressed in the stone. It shares the same 'hanan pacha' architectural style and prompts questions about the area's ancient past, as monkeys are not native to the region today.

**Getting there:** Situated below the Temple of the Moon in the Sacsayhuaman area, easily combined with a visit to the former. A 15-minute taxi from Cusco gets you to the area.
tags: ruins, solo, free, half-day, off-the-beaten-path, Sacsayhuaman, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Cheqtaqaqa Ruins
tagline: An easily accessible ruin right on the side of the road from Sacsayhuaman to Cusco. Its most fascina...
description:
An easily accessible ruin right on the side of the road from Sacsayhuaman to Cusco. Its most fascinating feature is a cave with evidence of vitrification, where the stone surface was turned to glass by extreme heat. Inside you'll find niches and a curious horseshoe-shaped stone bench.

**Getting there:** Located directly on the main road leading from Sacsayhuaman down to Cusco. It's an easy stop for a taxi or during a walk down from the main ruins.
tags: ruins, solo, free, quick-stop, off-the-beaten-path, geology, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Teteqaqa Ruins
tagline: A large ruin just 50 meters down the road from Cheqtaqaqa, popular with locals for its spectacular v...
description:
A large ruin just 50 meters down the road from Cheqtaqaqa, popular with locals for its spectacular views of Cusco. The site features mysterious forms carved into its surface and a small cave. It's a great, quick stop to appreciate the landscape.

**Getting there:** Found on the right side of the main road from Sacsayhuaman to Cusco, a very short walk from Cheqtaqaqa. Easily reachable by taxi or on foot.
tags: ruins, solo, free, quick-stop, viewpoint, Sacsayhuaman, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Grand Chincana, Chinchero
tagline: This site refers to the 'Hanan Pacha' huacas located below the main ticketed Chinchero ruins complex...
description:
This site refers to the 'Hanan Pacha' huacas located below the main ticketed Chinchero ruins complex. They can often be accessed for free by taking a side path, though one should be respectful of security. The area features intricate carvings on large stones.

**Getting there:** In Chinchero, take the path below the main church area, heading towards Pok Pok falls. Chinchero is a 45-minute colectivo ride or 30-minute taxi from Cusco.
tags: ruins, solo, free, off-the-beaten-path, Chinchero, hiking, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Ñaupa Iglesia
tagline: A highly mysterious and revered site featuring a bluestone rock with three carved seats and a stunni...
description:
A highly mysterious and revered site featuring a bluestone rock with three carved seats and a stunning, laser-precise 'portal' with recessed niches. Behind this is a cave. Accessing this powerful place requires a steep but short climb up agricultural terraces.

**Getting there:** Take a 20-minute taxi from Urubamba. From the road, it's a steep 10-15 minute walk up the stone terraces to reach the site.
tags: ruins, solo, free, off-the-beaten-path, spiritual, mysterious, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Inkilltambo Hike
tagline: A mysterious and rarely visited archaeological site perfect for quiet contemplation or a picnic lunc...
description:
A mysterious and rarely visited archaeological site perfect for quiet contemplation or a picnic lunch. It features beautiful 'hanan pacha' forms and a channel between monoliths with deep rectangular niches inside. Reaching the site requires a pleasant hike.

**Getting there:** Requires an approximately 40-minute hike. The trail can be started from the Temple of the Moon area or from an access point off Chinchaysuyo Avenue in Cusco.
tags: ruins, solo, free, off-the-beaten-path, hiking, half-day, meditation, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Zone X (Lanlakuyuq)
tagline: An unusual site in the Sacsayhuaman complex featuring numerous caves, tunnels, and carved niches. It...
description:
An unusual site in the Sacsayhuaman complex featuring numerous caves, tunnels, and carved niches. It has a reputation for a 'darker' energy and some past safety incidents, so visitors, especially those alone, should be cautious and aware of their surroundings.

**Getting there:** Part of the Sacsayhuaman complex just outside Cusco. You can get there by taxi or as part of a longer hike through the area's many ruins.
tags: ruins, solo, free, off-the-beaten-path, caves, tunnels, Sacsayhuaman, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Q'enko Chico
tagline: The smaller, free-to-access neighbor of the main Q'enko archaeological site. It boasts giant megalit...
description:
The smaller, free-to-access neighbor of the main Q'enko archaeological site. It boasts giant megalithic stones similar to those at Sacsayhuaman, intricate stonework, and a carved throne. The large grassy area makes it a perfect spot for a picnic with wonderful views of Cusco city.

**Getting there:** Located just below the main ticketed Q'enko site in Sacsayhuaman, right off the road leading down to Cusco. It's very easy to access by taxi or on foot.
tags: ruins, solo, free, off-the-beaten-path, picnic, viewpoint, Sacsayhuaman, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: Lazy Stones of Ollantaytambo
tagline: These are not a formal site, but a collection of giant, smoothly polished rose granite blocks scatte...
description:
These are not a formal site, but a collection of giant, smoothly polished rose granite blocks scattered along a road and in the town of Ollantaytambo. Known as 'Piedras Cansadas' (Tired Stones), they are believed to have been abandoned before reaching the main fortress, sparking many theories.

**Getting there:** At the main entrance of the Ollantaytambo ruins, take the road that goes to the left. The stones are littered along this path for anyone to see.
tags: ruins, solo, free, off-the-beaten-path, megaliths, geology, Ollantaytambo, solo:yes, off-the-beaten-path

title: LLaullipata Park Hike
tagline: A beautiful and free ecological park located just above Cusco. Perfect for a quiet morning hike away...
description:
A beautiful and free ecological park located just above Cusco. Perfect for a quiet morning hike away from the crowds to acclimatize to the altitude.

**Getting there:** Easily accessible on foot or via a short S/5 taxi ride from the historic center.
tags: park, nature, solo, half-day, free, off-the-beaten-path

title: Balcon del Diablo (Devil's Balcony)
tagline: A stunning natural cave and Inca site. The hike offers incredible views over Cusco and explores the ...
description:
A stunning natural cave and Inca site. The hike offers incredible views over Cusco and explores the Chacan Cave where the river flows directly through the rock.

**Getting there:** Walkable from Sacsayhuaman or accessible via taxi/colectivo.
tags: cave, ruins, hike, solo, half-day, free, off-the-beaten-path

title: Huchuy Qosqo Trek (DIY)
tagline: An 11-mile trek along an ancient Inca road leading to the remote Huchuy Qosqo ("Little Cusco") ruins...
description:
An 11-mile trek along an ancient Inca road leading to the remote Huchuy Qosqo ("Little Cusco") ruins. You will likely have the entire archaeological site to yourself.

**Getting there:** Take a colectivo to Tambomachay or Chinchero to start the trek, and end by hiking down to Lamay in the Sacred Valley.
tags: ruins, trek, solo, full-day, intense, off-the-beaten-path

title: Kinsa Cocha Lakes (Three Lakes)
tagline: A breathtaking hike around three high-altitude glacial lakes nestled in the Andes. Very few tourists...
description:
A breathtaking hike around three high-altitude glacial lakes nestled in the Andes. Very few tourists make it out here, offering a serene connection with nature.

**Getting there:** Hire a taxi from Pisac market (roughly S/60 round trip) to wait for you while you hike.
tags: lakes, nature, hike, solo, half-day, off-the-beaten-path

title: Cusco 4-Ruins Walk (Sacsayhuaman, Qenko, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay)
tagline: Explore the four magnificent Inca ruins perched immediately above Cusco. An excellent acclimatizatio...
description:
Explore the four magnificent Inca ruins perched immediately above Cusco. An excellent acclimatization day to see massive megalithic architecture, water temples, and ancient shrines.

**Getting there:** Take a colectivo or taxi up to Tambomachay (highest point) and walk downhill back to Cusco, visiting the sites along the way. Requires Boleto Turístico.
tags: ruins, inca, walk, solo, half-day, boleto-turistico

title: South Valley Ruins: Tipon and Piquillacta
tagline: Visit Tipon, a masterpiece of Inca water engineering and terracing, followed by Piquillacta, a massi...
description:
Visit Tipon, a masterpiece of Inca water engineering and terracing, followed by Piquillacta, a massive pre-Inca Wari city built entirely of adobe and stone.

**Getting there:** Take a public bus heading south towards Urcos from Cusco. Requires Boleto Turístico.
tags: ruins, water-temple, wari, inca, solo, half-day, boleto-turistico

title: Urquillos to Chinchero Hike
tagline: Hike the ancient path up to Chinchero.
description:
Start in the quiet town of Urquillos and hike the steep but beautiful ancient Inca trail up the mountain to reach the town of Chinchero. A fantastic physical challenge with rewarding views.

**Getting there:** Take a colectivo to Urquillos paradero. Hike ends in Chinchero where you can easily catch a bus back to Urubamba or Cusco.
tags: hike, ruins, off-the-beaten-path, half-day, free, half-day, local-vibe

title: Arin Waterfall & ALTO Cafe
tagline: A refreshing waterfall hike followed by creative Asian-inspired food.
description:
Take a gentle walk up to the beautiful Catarata de Arin. After enjoying the mist and nature, stroll back down to the pista and grab lunch at ALTO Cafe for fresh doughnuts and pad Thai.

**Getting there:** Take any Urubamba-Calca colectivo and ask to be dropped at the 2nd Paradero in Arin.
tags: waterfall, cafe, relax, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Yucay Terraces, Molino & Sonesta Breakfast
tagline: A luxurious breakfast followed by an exploration of grand Inca terraces.
description:
Start your morning with a hearty breakfast at the beautiful Sonesta Hotel cafe. Afterwards, walk up into the massive Inca agricultural terraces of Yucay and explore the ruins of the old Molino (mill).

**Getting there:** Yucay is just 10 minutes from Urubamba via taxi or a S/1 colectivo.
tags: breakfast, terraces, history, relax, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Urubamba Chullpas & Kampu Lunch
tagline: Hike to ancient tombs and enjoy the best curry in town.
description:
Hike up the valley side in Urubamba to explore 'Las Chullpas', ancient pre-Inca tombs built into the cliffside. Head back down to town and treat yourself to a massive bowl of curry at Kampu.

**Getting there:** The trailhead is walkable from the center of Urubamba.
tags: ruins, food, hike, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Huayna Capac Palace & Migas del Valle
tagline: Inca royal history paired with sourdough pizza.
description:
Explore the atmospheric, un-restored ruins of Inca Emperor Huayna Capac's palace on the edge of Urubamba. Afterwards, walk over to Migas del Valle for amazing sourdough bread, coffee, or pizza.

**Getting there:** Located on the outskirts of Urubamba; completely walkable or a S/3 mototaxi from the plaza.
tags: ruins, pizza, history, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Huayoccari & Yanacocha Lake
tagline: A steep ascent to a black lake, with a quiet town lunch.
description:
Tackle the steep, challenging hike up to Yanacocha (Black Lake) nestled high in the mountains above Huayoccari. Descend back to the peaceful village for a well-earned local lunch.

**Getting there:** Take a colectivo to the Huayoccari paradero between Urubamba and Calca.
tags: hike, lake, intense, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Huaran Quebrada & Viva Peru Cafe
tagline: A stunning valley walk ending with homemade ice cream.
description:
Walk up the scenic 'quebrada' (ravine) of Huaran, following the river deep into the mountains past local farms. Finish your walk at Viva Peru Cafe for a falafel bowl and their famous homemade ice cream.

**Getting there:** Drop off at Paradero Verde in Huaran via any Urubamba-Calca colectivo.
tags: hike, cafe, nature, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Calca Market & Garden Lunch
tagline: Bustling local commerce and a serene garden retreat.
description:
Dive into the authentic, bustling atmosphere of the Calca produce market—one of the best in the valley. Afterwards, escape the noise for a peaceful lunch at a local garden cafe like Del Campo or Pisonay.

**Getting there:** Calca is a major hub, easily accessible by colectivo from Urubamba, Pisac, or Cusco.
tags: market, culture, food, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Chinchero Market to Huaypo Lake Trout
tagline: Textile traditions and fresh lakeside dining.
description:
Spend the morning admiring the textiles and colors of the Chinchero market. Then, catch a ride out to the stunning Piuray or Huaypo lake and eat freshly caught trout cooked right on the shore.

**Getting there:** Requires a taxi from Chinchero to the lake, which can be negotiated in the plaza.
tags: market, food, lake, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Abra Malaga Pass Hot Chocolate
tagline: High-altitude views and the world's best hot chocolate.
description:
Take a spectacular drive up the winding mountain road past Ollantaytambo to the high pass of Abra Malaga. Bundle up, take in the glacier views, and stop at the tiny roadside shop for what locals swear is the best hot chocolate of your life.

**Getting there:** Hire a taxi from Ollantaytambo for a round trip to the pass.
tags: views, drive, food, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Pisac Back Trail & Altar Hummus
tagline: Hike a secret trail down from the famous ruins, then reward yourself with the best hummus in Peru.
description:
Skip the crowded main path and descend from the Pisac ruins via the tranquil 'back trail' for breathtaking, tourist-free views of the terraces. After your 90-minute hike, drop into Pisac's plaza and reward your efforts at Altar, a tiny gem serving up mind-blowing authentic hummus and warm, puffy flatbreads.

**Getting there:** Take a taxi (S/25) or mototaxi (S/10) to the top entrance of the ruins, then hike down to the plaza. No transport needed for the return.
tags: ruins, hiking, local-vibe, half-day, food, scenic-view, half-day, local-vibe

title: Ñaupa Iglesia Portal & Aiki Lunch
tagline: Explore a mysterious free ruin, then dine on unique Japanese-Andean cuisine in a tiny, 4-table restaurant.
description:
Discover the enigmatic Ñaupa Iglesia, a free and powerful site with a stunningly precise 'portal' carved into a cave face. After soaking in the energy, head to the sleepy town of Yucay for a truly special meal at Aiki, where chef Yuka works her magic with organic ingredients in her 'Japoandina' style. Booking ahead is essential for one of her four coveted tables.

**Getting there:** Take a colectivo towards Ollantaytambo from Urubamba and ask to be dropped at 'Pachar.' Cross the bridge; the ruin is a 15-min hike up. Afterwards, flag a colectivo on the main road to get to Yucay (5 mins).
tags: ruins, spiritual, local-vibe, foodie, off-the-beaten-path, half-day, half-day, local-vibe

title: Urubamba Market & Monkey Coffee
tagline: Dive into the sights and sounds of a real Andean market, then retreat to a cozy cafe for stellar coffee and falafel.
description:
Experience the authentic pulse of the valley at Urubamba's bustling main market, a colorful chaos of produce, cheeses, and local shoppers. Once your senses are full, duck down the street to Monkey Coffee, a local expat favorite, for a perfectly brewed coffee and their surprisingly delicious, garlicky falafel and baba ganoush.

**Getting there:** The market is in the center of Urubamba. Any mototaxi can take you there for S/3. Monkey Coffee is a 2-minute walk downhill from the market on Calle Huascar.
tags: local-vibe, market, food, half-day, coffee, relax, half-day, local-vibe
